subject: SLO & Benchmark blueprint: next steps and deliverables
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@streamlinehealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 23:10:00 +0000
Subject: SLO & Benchmark blueprint: next steps and deliverables

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run any bench work:

Summary of what you said on the call
- Target p95 latency: <= 120ms for standard chat requests (approx. 512-token input with streaming response).
- Sustained throughput target: ~300 requests/sec (peak bursts up to 600rps for 30s).
- Expected concurrent users at peak: ~120 active streams.
- Streaming is required (clients expect token-by-token flush).
- Accuracy/quality baseline: your internal QA will sign off based on the prompt set you provide.

What we need from you to proceed
1) Confirm the two latency SLOs: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 120ms for streaming with 512-token inputs.
2) Provide the representative prompt set (we suggested 200 prompts across short/medium/long) and a sample traffic profile (CSV or JSON) showing request size distribution and inter-arrival patterns.
3) Provide a 1–2 day window for us to run a reproducible benchmark (we recommend a 2-hour ramp + 4-hour steady-state run).
4) If you want us to run on a private VPC or dedicated pool, share network egress constraints and service-account for S3 bucket where you’ll drop traces.

Attached: sample_prompts_v1.jsonl (example prompt set) and traffic_profile_q1.csv (example arrival distribution).

Proposed Redwood deliverables
- Benchmark plan (detailed steps + measurement definitions) — draft attached as redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.md
- Reproducible harness: bash + Docker commands we’ll run and output artifacts (latency percentiles, QPS/time-series, token throughput, streaming flush latency).
- Short debrief with charts and recommended optimizations (batching, KV warmup strategy, quantization suggestion).

Can you confirm the SLO numbers and share the prompt set by EOD Friday PST? If yes, I’ll schedule the bench window and loop in our infra lead (Aditya).

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom_das@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

----
Attachment stubs: sample_prompts_v1.jsonl (JSONL), traffic_profile_q1.csv (CSV), redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.md (Markdown)

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@streamlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 02:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark blueprint: next steps and deliverables

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the SLOs look right overall but a few clarifications:
- p95 <= 120ms is for end-to-end response with streaming enabled (we mean time-to-first-token + sustained token latency; most of our payloads are short responses ~50–150 tokens).
- We do want the platform to support backfill/async inference for large-batch nightly jobs but that’s a separate flow not in this benchmark.
- Throughput target: 300 sustained rps is correct; bursts to 600rps expected during business hours.
- Concurrency: the 120 active streams estimate is good; those are long-lived (~30s/session) on average.

Attached are two files: sample_prompts_v1.jsonl (we edited a few sensitive examples out) and traffic_profile_q1.csv (per-minute counts).

Questions from our infra/QA team before you run:
1) How do you measure streaming latency? Do you report time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and token flush intervals?
2) Will your harness warm the KV cache / model weights ahead of steady-state runs?
3) We need a repeatable seed for RNGs to reproduce any sampling variance — can you include that in the plan?

If you can send the benchmark plan with measurement definitions (TTFB, token-lag, token-throughput, tail-latency calc method) we’ll review and provide sign-off. Also include the minimal infra spec so our procurement team can confirm capacity for a Dedicated run if needed.

– Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering | Streamline Health
j.ellis@streamlinehealth.com

Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark blueprint: next steps and deliverables

Jordan —

Great, thanks for the files and the specific questions. Short answers up front and I’ve pasted the draft measurement section below — that will be in more detail in redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.md (attached).

Quick answers
- Streaming latency: we report time-to-first-token (TTFT), token-flush interval distribution (time between application-visible token events), and aggregated end-to-end percentiles computed from request start to final token committed.
- Warmup: yes — we run a configurable warmup that primes KV cache and forces at least one full model weight load. We recommend a 30-minute warmup at 10% traffic, then ramp to steady state.
- RNG reproducibility: we will run with deterministic sampling seeds where possible and capture the seed in the run metadata (we’ll include the exact commit hash + seed).

DRAFT: Measurement definitions (excerpt)
- Request start: client-side timestamp when HTTP POST is sent.
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): delta between request start and timestamp of first byte received by client.
- Token-flush interval: inter-token arrival intervals; report median and 95/99 tails.
- End-to-end latency: time from request start to final token received; report p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Throughput/QPS: successful completed requests per second (exclude 5xx).
- Error rate: percent of requests with non-200 or malformed stream.
- Reproducibility artifacts: raw timing logs (ndjson), run manifest (commit, seed, infra spec), and aggregated summary CSV.

Proposed bench window
- Candidate: Mon Feb 16, 02:00–08:00 UTC (we’ll ask for a 6-hour block; plan includes 30m warmup, 90m ramp, 3hr steady-state 300rps, 30m cool-down).

Minimal infra spec (for Dedicated)
- 8x A100 (or equivalent vCPU/GPU ratio) in a single region, 10Gbps NIC, autoscaling disabled for the run.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the bench window above (Mon 16)?
2) Grant a temporary S3 bucket path or Drive folder with the final prompt set and a target acceptance criteria doc (QA pass/fail rules).
3) We’ll prepare a run script and share a reproducibility checklist with the exact commands to run — you’ll be able to replay the run in your environment if desired.

I’ve attached the draft bench plan (redwood_benchmark_plan_v1.md) — it contains the full commands and expected outputs.

If this looks good I’ll lock the window and ping Aditya to provision capacity.

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: SLO & Benchmark blueprint: next steps and deliverables

Looping in a couple of quick operational notes before we lock the run:

1) KV-cache warmup details — we should include an explicit precondition that the run starts only after 95% of workers report a warmed cache sample. We’ve seen several false failures where incomplete warmup inflated p95.

2) Tail measurement — when reporting p99, include both client-side and server-side (inferred) timings so we can separate network variance from model compute.

3) Failure budget & pass criteria — propose the following pass rule for the pilot: during the 3-hour steady state, p95 <= 120ms and error rate < 0.5%. If p95 is slightly above but error rate is zero, we still require a root-cause review before sign-off.

4) Communication — I’ll produce a single-slide summary that Jordan can share with procurement (capacity & cost estimate).

Once Jordan confirms the window and uploads the final prompt set, we’ll proceed.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
